question: Suppose $f(x)$ is strictly increasing in $(a, b)$ and $g(x)$ is strictly decreasing in $(a, b)$. For which of the following functions is the derivative negative for all $x$ in $(a, b)$?
explanation:
Since f(x) is strictly increasing, f'(x) > 0.

Since g(x) is strictly decreasing, g'(x) < 0.

Option A: h'(x) = f'(x) + g'(x). This can be positive or negative.

Option B: h'(x) = f'(x) − g'(x). Since −g'(x) > 0, this is always positive.

Option C: h'(x) = −f'(x) + g'(x). Here −f'(x) < 0 and g'(x) < 0, so their sum is always negative.

Option D: h'(x) = −f'(x) − g'(x). Since −f'(x) < 0 and −g'(x) > 0, the result can be positive or negative.

Therefore, only option C is always negative.
